question: Should exact requester consumption permanently suppress descendant delivery retries even when the requester's final outward delivery fails?
rationale: The code can implement either model, but source inspection cannot decide whether OpenClaw's product contract defines delivery at requester consumption or only at eventual user-visible delivery.

options.title: Use a distinct consumed state
options.body: Record requester consumption as terminal descendant accounting without claiming user-visible delivery, while the requester result remains responsible for outward delivery.

options.title: Treat consumption as delivered
options.body: Accept the PR's model that exact, scoped requester consumption is sufficient delivery proof and suppresses later descendant retry.

options.title: Defer to durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this PR and solve requester consumption within the broader durable completion inbox or spool design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Use a distinct consumed state
recommendation.body: Record requester consumption as terminal descendant accounting without claiming user-visible delivery, while the requester result remains responsible for outward delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available recent-history routing candidate across the central cron fallback and persisted registry surfaces.
